raw:
{SA} ZAR FX – post CPI:

June CPI figures accelerated beyond market’s expectations with both the headline (5% y/y) and core (4.1% y/y) numbers exceeding expectations. Fuel prices, transport, housing and some services components surprised on the upside, indicating the upswing in inflation is spilling over from just the oil related one. The CPI release confirmed SARB’s comments about the second-round effects already filtering through the pricing behavior in the country.

We have seen some aggressive paying on FX swaps post numbers, and we have faded the spike in the FX swaps, especially the front-end. Heavy coupon payments will be hitting the market at the end of the month and with the 25bp hike now fully priced it, it offers a good risk reward to go received up to 3m area.

Spot-wise, we saw some knee-jerk $ demand post the release. However, inter-bank market faded above 16.50 yet again, focusing on a more hawkish reaction function from the SARB and ignoring sharply higher oil prices. I bought some USDZAR on this dip and will be looking for a retest of 16.65 in the coming sessions. Higher SARB’s rates path is a result of a supply shock, not a higher growth related one, and it is far from obvious to me that this should be positive for the currency.
